evidence.title: First API Request
evidence.challenge: Create and send a first GET request in Postman, inspect the response, and confirm the method, URL, and successful HTTP status.

answers.observation: Postman sent the request to retrieve the URL https://postman-echo.com/get.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: See Client → Request → Server → Response
evidence.challenge: Now you will connect the API mental model to something you can actually see in Postman.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Send GET and POST Requests
evidence.challenge: Send both GET and POST requests, confirm successful responses, and explain the different action each method performed.

answers.methodMeaning: the get request retrieved a tree. the post created a trigger.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Build Query Parameters
evidence.challenge: Build a GET request with query parameters, send it successfully, and verify that the expected parameter values appear in the response.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Send and Inspect a Header
evidence.challenge: Add a custom HTTP header in Postman, send the request, and verify in the echoed response that the header name and value were transmitted.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Send JSON in a Request Body
evidence.challenge: Send a POST request with a valid JSON body, verify the returned JSON data, and confirm the request used application/json.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Compare Success and Failure
evidence.challenge: Compare a successful request with a deliberately missing endpoint and use the 200 and 404 responses as troubleshooting evidence.

answers.meaning: there's a problem with the request. "Requested resource could not be found."

evidence.title: Guided Lab: See How Authorization Is Sent
evidence.challenge: Configure Bearer-token authentication in Postman, identify the Authorization header, and explain the difference between authentication and authorization.

answers.difference: Authentication proves possession of credential while authorization establishes what the entity is allow to do/access.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Replace a Hard-Coded URL With a Variable
evidence.challenge: Create a base_url environment variable, use it in a request instead of hard-coding the host, and verify that the variable-based request succeeds.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Turn Requests Into a Repeatable Workflow
evidence.challenge: Organize existing requests into a Core Diagnostics folder so related diagnostic work is repeatable and easier to navigate.

evidence.title: Guided Lab: Write Your First Automated Test
evidence.challenge: Add an automated status-code test, confirm it passes for the expected 200 response, deliberately make the expectation wrong, and verify that the test detects the failure.

answers.lesson: it proved that the test detects when the actual response does not match the expected result

evidence.title: Guided Investigation: Reproduce → Compare → Fix
evidence.challenge: Reproduce a 404 failure, compare it with a known-good request, identify the URL path as the relevant difference, correct it, and verify the request returns 200.

answers.rootCause: problem with the request or authorization context, defect in the URL
answers.fix: updated the end of the URL to get instead of test

evidence.title: Support Case: Customer Filter Is Missing
evidence.challenge: Reproduce a customer's incomplete filtered request, identify the missing status parameter from the evidence, correct the request, and document the fix.

answers.supportNote: customer's request was missing status parameter. added status = open to query params, sent the request again, and verified args show customer id = 42 and status = open.

evidence.title: Capstone: Reproduce, Test, Diagnose, and Fix
evidence.challenge: Start from a known-good request, introduce one controlled endpoint failure, use the response and automated test as evidence, diagnose the cause, correct it, and verify the request succeeds again.

answers.rootCause: response did not match the expected status due to incorrect endpoint path
answers.summary:
symptom: working request started returning a 404 after I changed the endpoint path.

evidence: before the change the request returned 200 OK and the status test passed but after changing the endpoint the request returned 404 not found and the test failed because it was still expecting 200.

root cause: the endpoint pass was wrong.

fix: i restored the request to the correct /post endpoint.

verification: after restoring the correct endpoint the request returned 200 OK again and the status test passed.
answers.diagnosis: I chose to correct the endpoint URL, the status and test changed based on the endpoint path used.
